slot.brief: Solve a trigonometric equation of the form a cos x + b sin x = c or a sum-to-product type and write the general solution.

stem: The general solution, for real $x$, of $\cos 3x+\cos x=\sin 2x$ is:

verdicts.working: Use cos 3x + cos x = 2 cos 2x cos x. Then cos x(cos 2x − sin x) = 0. Thus cos x = 0, or with sin x = t, 1 − 2t² = t, giving t = 1/2 or −1. These yield exactly the solutions in (A).

working:
$\cos 3x+\cos x=2\cos 2x\cos x$, so $2\cos x(\cos 2x-\sin x)=0$.
$\cos x=0\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}+k\pi$.
$\cos 2x=\sin x\Rightarrow 1-2\sin^2x=\sin x\Rightarrow (2\sin x-1)(\sin x+1)=0$.
$\sin x=\dfrac12\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{\pi}{6}+2k\pi$ or $\dfrac{5\pi}{6}+2k\pi$; $\sin x=-1$ is already included.

Independent check: Use cos 3x + cos x = 2 cos 2x cos x. Then cos x(cos 2x − sin x) = 0. Thus cos x = 0, or with sin x = t, 1 − 2t² = t, giving t = 1/2 or −1. These yield exactly the solutions in (A).
solution:
Using $\\cos 3x+\\cos x=2\\cos 2x\\cos x$, the equation becomes
$$2\\cos x(\\cos 2x-\\sin x)=0.$$
Thus $\\cos x=0$ gives $x=\\frac{\\pi}{2}+k\\pi$. Otherwise, $1-2\\sin^2x=\\sin x$, so $\\sin x=\\frac12$ or $-1$; these give $x=\\frac{\\pi}{6}+2k\\pi$, $\\frac{5\\pi}{6}+2k\\pi$, with $\\sin x=-1$ already included above.
